text:
ash: Heads up — seeing a new pattern: lots of tiny GPU pods stuck Pending in eu-west1 for ~30m. They land on nodes with rack-isolated taints and never get scheduled. cc @kevin @jess
kevin: Which taint exactly? any node affinity from the pods?
jess: Might be warmpool/reserve padding + thin-shelf fragmentation. we've seen small pods get stuck if binpack prefers large slots. :thinking:
ash: From a node describe (cropped):
```
Taints: rack-isolated=true:NoSchedule
Labels: gpu-type=nvidia-a100, shelf=thin, warmpool=true
Allocatable: nvidia.com/gpu=1
Pods: 12/12 (some non-gpu system pods)
```
kevin: ok so nodes are tiny and mostly saturated by system pods. Scheduler is skipping due to taint + affinity. Any recent changes to taint rollout?
ash: Not afaik. No recent taint rollouts in eu-west1. We did increase warmpool padding last week for a canary.
peter: Also check network readiness timeouts — we had conntrack exhaustion in eu-west1-c earlier and kubelet reported slow pod lifecycle -> delays in releasing stale allocations. That could amplify fragmentation.
jess: If conntrack caused kubelet lag, pods might be reported terminating but not freeing the GPU resource, so scheduler thinks there's no room.
ops-bot: ALERT: GPU eviction spike: 400 evictions in 10m (eu-west1) — triggered at 2026-03-21T10:12:00Z
kevin: Yikes. Two paths: immediate — bump warm pool size or temporarily relax rack-isolated taint (change NoSchedule -> PreferNoSchedule) to let scheduler place on other racks. Longer — run a compacting job to defrag thin shelves and reduce small-slot fragmentation.
ash: Cost question: relaxing taints risks noisy-neighbor perf regressions. Compacting involves draining a cluster subset which will incur short-term preempts/evictions. Which is less bad?
jess: For customer-facing low-latency inference, noisy neighbors are worse. For batch/off-peak, compacting is fine. We should target non-critical pools for drain.
peter: Quick triage steps: 1) check kubelet pod eviction deadlines and node conditions 2) run conntrack reclaim on affected AZ 3) temporarily increase warm pool by +20% for 1h and monitor.
kevin: If we want a fast scheduler tweak: try adding this scheduler plugin override to prefer coalescing small pods: 
```yaml
apiVersion: kubescheduler.config.k8s.io/v1
kind: KubeSchedulerConfiguration
profiles:
  - plugins:
      score:
        enabled: 
          - name: PodTopologySpread
          - name: BinpackingScore # pseudo-plugin for example
```
(not a real quick fix but idea)
ash: I'll bump warmpool +20% for eu-west1 canary now, run conntrack reclaim, and open a compacting run template for next maintenance window.
jess: Sounds good. Also add a telemetry query to count "gpu-pending > 5m" per AZ so we can alert earlier.
kevin: +1. if warm-pool bump doesn't help in 30m, we'll consider softening taints on a per-rack basis and coordinate on perf tests.
ash: executing warm-pool bump and conntrack reclaim now. Will report back in ~25m. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: NOTE: Scheduled maintenance window available tonight 02:00-04:00 UTC (can use for compacting run)
ash: thanks — added to the compacting run doc.
kevin: appreciated.
